title: Qiskit SDK v2.6 release summary
content: Quantum Research Blog Qiskit SDK v2.6 release summary Technical release summary for Qiskit SDK v2.6, including updates on top new features, breaking changes, and our ongoing efforts to make Qiskit the world's most performant quantum SDK. Date 22 Oct 2026 Authors Qiskit Team Topics Software Updates Qiskit Share this blog Was this blog post helpful? Yes No Key takeaways: Qiskit SDK v2.6 is a C API–focused release, bringing the compiler's pass-manager framework, QPY serialization, and custom operations to compiled languages. A new C API pass-manager framework lets you write custom compiler passes and lower circuits through multiple type-checked intermediate representations. QPY serialization is now in the C API, enabling programs in other languages including C, C++, and Julia to save and exchange circuits compatible with Python's qiskit.qpy . You can define custom quantum operations, including hardware-native gates, directly from the C API without Python's object model. Qiskit v2.6 makes progress toward enabling use of the C API in environments where Python isn't installed. QPY format v18 is now the default and shrinks serialized circuits; minimum Python stays 3.10, source builds need Rust 1.89. We're excited to announce the release of Qiskit SDK v2.6! The latest minor release in the v2.x series continues our effort to strengthen the SDK's core infrastructure—making it faster, more extensible, and more capable as a high-performance compiler for quantum computing. A central story of recent releases has been Qiskit's evolution beyond Python, exposing its high-performance Rust core through a C API that interoperates with nearly every language and opens the door to the tightly-coupled, quantum-centric supercomputing (QCSC) workflows that HPC environments demand. Qiskit v2.6 is, above all, a C API release: it brings the compiler's pass-manager framework, QPY serialization, and custom operations to the C API, and continues the behind-the-scenes work of making it possible to use the C API without having Python installed. These capabilities are more than conveniences for non-Python users. A compiler that lowers a program through multiple intermediate representations, a serialization format that moves circuits between languages and systems, and an execution model that puts composable control in the user's hands—these are the foundational plumbing for what's next. That groundwork points toward the QCSC and fault-tolerant workloads to come, even as Qiskit keeps delivering real value for near-term work today. Qiskit is being built to be the performant software stack users reach for across that entire continuum—not only for near-term work, where it already delivers real value, but for the error-corrected pipelines as well. The TL;DR Qiskit SDK v2.6 is a release centered on the C API. Previous releases gave C API users the ability to build circuits and run them through Qiskit's transpiler; v2.6 gives them far more control—a customizable, extensible pass-manager framework (including lowering through multiple IRs), QPY serialization, and the ability to define their own operations—all without Python. Highlights include: A new pass-manager framework in the C API. You can now write and execute compiler passes directly from C, and lower a program through multiple intermediate representations (IRs) with type-checked, cross-language pipelines. QPY serialization in the C API. Qiskit's portable binary circuit format can now be written and read from C, operating on native circuits without a Python round-trip, and remaining compatible with Python-produced QPY. Custom operations defined from C. You can now fully define quantum operations directly from the C API and add them to any circuit. Continued progress toward making Python optional. Behind-the-scenes work moves the standalone C library closer to running without Python being installed—a stepping stone toward, for example, letting Julia-on-Windows users run Qiskit . A new QPY format version (v18). 2.6 bumps the QPY format with several improvements (see Upgrade considerations). Top new features and improvements New pass-manager framework in the C API Qiskit v2.6 introduces a generic pass-manager framework to the C API. C API users could already run Qiskit's preset transpilation pipeline; now they can build their own—writing individual compiler passes and composing them into custom pass managers, all from compiled languages. The new QkPassManager manages execution. It can be populated with QkPass objects via qk_passmanager_push_pass and run with qk_passmanager_run_simple ; the pass manager and its passes report errors through QkCompilationError . The functionality of a pass is defined through a vtable ( QkPassVtable ). Passes declare their input and output IR with a QkIrHandle , which can describe either a dynamically defined C IR or a built-in Qiskit IR (today, QkCircuit and QkDag ). The pass manager uses these handles to verify the pipeline—enabling type-checked compiler pipelines .
